openings.claim: Use the supplied evidence-ledger function alone: each pair receives a row containing its earliest supported divergent stage or unresolved interval, cited record identifiers, observed mismatch separately from explanation, uncertainty, and a resource-fitting next check.
openings.delta: Change the claim carrier from an incident-review narrative with a reference appendix, the nearest ordinary rival, to a claim-linked ledger. During final review, mark removed supporting records unavailable and withdraw affected definite claims unless surviving supplied records independently support them. Manifest membership cannot replace evidence of execution.
openings.prediction: Compared with the narrative rival, the ledger may leave fewer unsupported definite claims after transform-record removal while retaining surviving supported claims. Differing observations are unsupported-claim counts, correct boundaries or covering unresolved intervals against sealed answers, and citations that survive removal. This is an unmeasured prediction.
openings.probe: Assign one disjoint three-pair subset to each variant. Budget ten minutes per pair within the sixty minutes, at most ten initial manual inspections and two final-review inspections, logging every inspection including rereads. Apply the stipulated random removal during final review; freeze all six outputs before opening the two sealed answer sheets. Use the additional twenty minutes to compare correctness, uncertainty, surviving support and inspection counts. Report stage-order/timestamp conflict as uncertainty, without using timestamp order as an unsupported stage claim. If the remaining inspection capacity cannot establish the earliest boundary, report an unresolved interval and a bounded next check.
assumptions: Ledger writing uses the supplied spreadsheet or local script environment; no additional records or system access are required.

Defeat conditions include no unsupported-claim improvement, loss of otherwise supported boundaries, or budget overruns. Disjoint subsets and only two disturbed pairs limit attribution; subset difficulty can explain differences.

assessment: A bounded probe of claim traceability, not deployment or demonstrated divergence detection. The ledger organizes supplied support; effectiveness and subset comparability remain uncertain.
